items.content_html:

Nuxalk Nation leaders say the grizzly attack that killed Jennifer Balcarras and her daughter, Selah Reed, near Bella Coola has renewed trauma in a community still recovering from a separate bear attack last year. The British Columbia Conservation Officer Service said forensic evidence linked a female grizzly and her three yearling cubs to the deaths. The bears were killed, and investigators believe the attack likely involved rare predatory behaviour. Elected Chief Tlhmtimut Samuel Schooner said community support services would remain available for as long as needed. The Nuxalk Nation thanked conservation officers for resolving the incident, while saying the deaths had reopened trauma from the previous attack. Authorities also confirmed the four bears were not involved in that earlier attack, which injured 11 people.

items.title: [elpais.com] Cyberattacks on refrigeration systems fuel concerns about connected household appliances
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Cyberattacks on internet-connected refrigeration systems in supermarkets and French blood banks have destroyed food in Europe and heightened concerns about connected devices. Nearly 800 freezers were sabotaged in France and Northern Europe this week. On November 2, temperatures also rose in the cold rooms of a blood donation service in France. There, alarms and swift action prevented damage to stored blood. The targeted systems used internet-accessible controls for maintenance and remote operation. According to experts, similar attacks on private smart-home devices are less likely because, with typical router configurations, the devices cannot be accessed directly from the internet. Risks include outdated software, weak passwords, and devices with cameras or microphones. Germany’s Federal Office for Information Security recommends automatic updates, separate networks for smart-home devices, and unique passwords. The identity of those behind the attacks remains unclear.

items.title: [thehackernews.com] Grok Build exposes 35,578 apps, leaking sensitive company data
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Security researchers found that 35,578 of 37,571 web apps built with SpaceXSI’s Grok Build, a chat-based app builder, were accessible without signing in, exposing business and personal information at SpaceXSI and 30 other organizations. Claroc, the security firm that found the apps, estimated that about one in 10 accessible apps contained internal or personal data and roughly 2% held material it rated high or critical in severity. Exposed material included a SpaceXSI sales map covering 594 strategic accounts, a hospital directory listing more than 3,500 employees, an intensive-care briefing about a patient and a timesheet with 18 users’ passwords in its code. The apps’ addresses were discoverable through searchable passive DNS records, and Grok Build preselected “Anyone with the link” as the sharing option in the researchers’ test. SpaceXSI removed 24 apps made by its own staff and X employees; Claroc said other users’ apps remained available and that it had begun contacting affected organizations.

items.title: [farmer.pl] Farmers urged to shred corn stalks to curb pests and disease
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

As Poland’s corn harvest continues, agronomic guidance recommends finely shredding stalks and other crop residues after harvest to reduce winter shelter for the European corn borer and limit disease in the next season. The borer’s larvae overwinter in stalks, while feeding damage can promote Fusarium infections that contaminate grain with mycotoxins. Residue management also affects soil organic matter: grain corn leaves substantial biomass in the field, while silage harvesting removes nearly all above-ground material. Guidance recommends accounting for soil moisture and the next crop; working wet soil can cause compaction, and fields vulnerable to erosion may need residue left on the surface.

Anthropic said it based the determination on expectations for future models and its overall rate of progress, not on behavior observed in current models. According to a police complaint, two Mumbai-based non-bank lenders lost about $2 million in more than 700 unauthorized transfers on Oct. 8 and 9 after attackers compromised APIs. Reports on that incident did not establish a link to Crafty Falcon (firstpost.com, reddit.com). Tools named: CERT-In identified the AI-assisted tools ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI; researchers have linked at least two to China, but the agency has not named a country behind the campaign (firstpost.com, reddit.com). Test transfers: The attackers reportedly use very small transfers to test unauthorized payment routes before attempting larger withdrawals, and target cryptocurrency services to steal wallet keys and funds (theregister.com, thehackernews.com). ARTEX image downloads: Docker Hub statistics showed the backdoored ARTEX image had been downloaded 9,000 times (thehackernews.com). Reporting deadline: Financial institutions were told to report serious incidents to CERT-In and the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) within six hours, using the RBI’s DAKSH portal (newskart.com).
